title: Object hero: the product is the page
summary: One featured product presented as a specimen, with the details and buy control in a single purchase block.

layout.skeleton: 7/5 split; the product image sits left, offset 1 column, and overlaps into a facts band
layout.focus: the featured product and one supplied detail that helps a buyer choose it, such as a tasting note, material, or finish
layout.desktop: Put the product name at the image edge. Give the deciding detail its own line. Keep the remaining facts and the add control together on the same column edges.
layout.mobile: At 390 px, use a shallow product crop up to 35% of the visible height. Keep the product name, deciding detail, size, price, supplied purchase facts, and add control together in reading order. Put the action in flow so it cannot cover a fact.
layout.rhythm: 96px between bands; the ledger uses a 24px baseline

imagery.subject: the product on a plain surface. If it has a label, make the product name and supplied variant or size the strongest lettering.
imagery.crop: tight, with the product cut by the right edge
imagery.fallback: Use the product name and its deciding detail as specimen typography when product imagery is unavailable.

motion.effect: bag count ticks and the pill settles 4px

action.instruction: One primary action attached to the product. Fill it from the brief's product, size and price, and never repeat it in a hero band
action.label: Add [product], [size] — [price]

why: A first-time buyer needs one choice, not a catalogue. Making the object the hero and stating the brief's exact facts reads warm and exact.

sources.observation: Agrumea Farm hero: the product jars are the hero on cream paper with an oxblood shape and type set on a curve; the only CTA is a small pill on the featured jar ('Scopri il prodotto').

credit: Agrumea Farm site (Awwwards submission; designer not verified)

title: Exception first: the problem owns the screen
summary: The most urgent item is promoted out of the list into a full-width strip, with its position in the queue; every other row stays quiet. Use for time-pressured operations queues.

layout.skeleton: exception strip on top (item ID, location, deviation), the full queue table below, a due-next rail on the right
layout.focus: the deviation value at 40px tabular figures, with an 'n / total' position label
layout.desktop: 12-col; strip spans 12, table 8, rail 4 holding the next item due
layout.mobile: strip, then rail, then table as stacked rows

imagery.subject: none; location codes act as the visuals
imagery.fallback: location code set at 24px tabular figures

motion.effect: the value cross-fades; the strip edge pulses once

action.instruction: Focus jumps the table filter to the exception. Fill it from the brief's most urgent item
action.label: Focus [item ID] at [location]

why: An operator on the clock should see the one problem before the list. Calm comes from making everything except the exception quiet.

sources.observation: Linear's home page product mock (server HTML) shows one focused issue 'DRV-8852' with a '1 / 84' queue position, a sidebar of 'Inbox | My issues | Reviews', and a properties rail ('In Progress | Medium | Karri'): one item in focus, its place in the queue, and its state beside it.

credit: Linear (Linear Orbit), home page product mock

title: Stage call sheet
summary: A working stage document. Put the room list on warm paper and mark the delayed room directly in its row. The list is the main composition.

layout.skeleton: Print-like masthead, then a single ruled cue ledger. Pair the room name and the actual status across the rule. Apply the accent to the delayed row's status cell and keep the ready row quiet.
layout.focus: A large room name beside a compact burgundy status cell showing the actual delay. No copy of the exception above the list and no secondary rail repeating room status.
layout.desktop: Align the masthead and ledger on one edge. Give the room name three quarters of the row with a narrow, consistently aligned status column. Place the filter above the ledger.
layout.mobile: Masthead, filter, then the same two-column ledger in document order. Wrap the status before squeezing the room name. Each room appears once.
layout.rhythm: Wide gap after the masthead. Thin rules and square edges mark the ledger. Use compact control text and generous row height.

imagery.subject: The room names and cue marks carry the visual identity.
imagery.crop: No image slot for the operations view.
imagery.fallback: Use real room names and thin typographic rules.

motion.trigger: The stage manager changes the room filter.
motion.effect: Fade the newly updated row list in from .78 opacity. Focus stays on the filter and the live status announces the new room count.
motion.reduced: Apply filter and status immediately with the same focus behavior.

action.instruction: Use two pressed-state buttons above the rows to choose the full room list or delays only. The same control switches the list back. Retain each room's exact supplied status.
action.label: Delayed only

why: Stage management reads a cue against its corresponding information. Aligning each delay with its room reduces scanning while the paper, rules, and cue color relate the tool to that work.

sources.observation: The Prompt Book explains that the deputy stage manager uses the book to run rehearsals. It describes cues set opposite the corresponding script lines with lines connecting each cue to its trigger. The color palette and filter treatment are original adaptations.

title: Platform sign: departure as signage
summary: Time and place set like a station sign; the credential opens in one tap. Use for on-the-move transit, tickets or boarding.

layout.skeleton: one station sign for the current departure, followed by its ticket action and a quieter list of other choices
layout.focus: time, destination and platform form one compact unit a moving rider can read at a glance
layout.desktop: Use a narrow centered lane. Keep the destination and platform badge close to the time. Let the sign height follow its content.
layout.mobile: At 390 px group the time, destination and platform above a full-width ticket control. When the brief supplies a later option, show its time on the closed row so the rider can compare without opening it.

motion.effect: the credential slides up from the sign band to show the code

action.instruction: The button names the credential from the brief, not 'View'
action.label: Show ticket [ticket ID]

why: A walking rider reads at a glance. Signage-scale numerals and a single reveal beat card-stacked layouts for speed.

sources.observation: GOV.UK: 'Write button text in sentence case, describing the action it performs.'
.typography-body is 17px at -0.022em, a readable body floor.

title: Ground plane: full-bleed built work
summary: The lead project opens as a full-bleed site photograph under a serif title; the other projects sit small and off the grid. Use for spatial practices.

layout.skeleton: full-bleed lead project; title split across two lines; secondary projects offset at 1/3 width; contact in a quiet footer
layout.focus: lead project title at 120px, with its scale and completion year from the brief
layout.desktop: Title bottom-left on an opaque paper panel overlapping the image edge. Facts align in a right-hand column.
layout.mobile: image at 70vh; title below it, not overlaid
layout.rhythm: 160px section gaps; empty space as the material

imagery.subject: the built site at ground or eye level, with planting or material in the foreground
imagery.fallback: site-plan line drawing in ink on paper

motion.effect: the image scales 1.04 to 1 (the one signature move)

action.instruction: Primary link opens the lead case study; contact is plain text
action.label: Open the [project] case study

why: Spacious and material: built work needs room. A serif display paired with a quiet sans and a full-bleed ground reads as real work, not a template.

sources.observation: Studio Dado (viewed): the serif display 'FORM FOLLOWS FEELING' is set full-bleed over warm material photography, with a small sans nav on an offset grid.
Studio D live HTML: 'Spatial design at eye level', positioning spatial practice in plain words.

title: Scale ledger: plans as stops on one quantity
summary: Plans are compared along the single quantity buyers pay for, not shown as identical cards. Use when tiers differ mainly by an amount.

layout.skeleton: a horizontal bar from 0 to the largest tier's quantity, with each plan as a stop; feature differences listed under each stop
layout.focus: the recommended middle stop, labelled with its quantity and key feature
layout.desktop: bar spans 10 cols, with stops placed proportionally; prices sit above the stops
layout.mobile: bar turns vertical; stops become rows
layout.rhythm: 12px base; 48px between the bar and the details

imagery.subject: none; the bar is the image

motion.effect: the fill moves to the stop

action.instruction: Continue with the chosen plan, naming the plan and price from the brief
action.label: Continue with [plan] — [price]/[period]

why: Buyers pay for a quantity. One proportional scale makes the choice legible, and naming the plan and price on the button is assured, not loud.

sources.observation: GOV.UK: button text should describe 'the action it performs'.

title: Margin front: feature at reading width
summary: The lead story runs at reading width with an italic deck; secondary items run in a narrow margin column. Use for small editorial homes.

layout.skeleton: feature title across 8 cols, standfirst at 62ch; a 3-col margin column holds the secondary dispatch and a recipe card
layout.focus: feature title, with byline and read time from the brief
layout.desktop: asymmetric 8/1/3 split; the title breaks into the margin
layout.mobile: feature first, then dispatch, then recipe

imagery.subject: the feature's setting or material, top-down
imagery.fallback: an ink rule plus a large italic drop numeral of the read time

motion.trigger: Open the feature by tap or keyboard
motion.effect: Reveal the standfirst and underline the active link as the reading view opens
motion.reduced: Open the reading view immediately and preserve focus

action.instruction: Headline and button both open the feature
action.label: Read [feature title]

why: Tactile, observant reading wants a comfortable measure and print logic: rules, margins and an italic voice instead of card grids.

sources.observation: Butterick: 'Aim for an average line length of 45–90 characters, including spaces.'

title: Constraint comparison
summary: Put the two measured fit limits beside the available choices and keep a withdrawn selection visible until the visitor chooses a replacement.

layout.skeleton: Open with one shared dimensional datum, then a ruled choice comparison; keep the current selection and ready time beside the replacement decision.
layout.focus: The supplied height limit and swing limit shown as separate measured cues beside each tool's actual fit evidence.
layout.desktop: Set the cabinet datum and the two constraint readings across the opening. Below, align each tool's assembled height, required swing, readiness and selection control on consistent rules. Keep a withdrawn selection named until the visitor selects another tool.
layout.mobile: At 390px keep the selected tool, withdrawal reason, readiness time and replacement choices in the first view. Show height in mm with its supplied tolerance and swing in degrees as separate cues. Verify at 320px without hiding an action. State that unmeasured hand clearance remains uncertain.
layout.rhythm: Use a 12px rule grid, compact comparison rows and one generous break after the shared datum. No repeated cards.

imagery.subject: A dimension line and small swing arc drawn only from the supplied geometry.
imagery.crop: Keep the dimensional datum connected to the choice rows; do not imply a product photo or inventory image.
imagery.fallback: Use type, rules and a simple dimension line. Identify any physical clearance the brief does not measure.

motion.trigger: The visitor chooses a replacement tool.
motion.effect: Move the selection marker to the chosen row and update one adjacent selection status.
motion.reduced: Change the marker and status immediately.

action.instruction: Keep the withdrawn choice visible with the reason supplied by the brief. Offer only supplied alternatives and let the visitor make the replacement selection.
action.label: Choose [tool]

why: A borrower making a fit decision needs the shared scale and both independent constraints beside the actual alternatives. A shared datum helps visitors reconcile evidence across the alternatives before choosing.

sources.observation: Vessel distinguishes assembled screwdriver geometry and states a 6-degree ratchet swing. This is a reference for presenting two measured properties; it does not identify any item in the fixture as Vessel inventory.
The observed page separates its globe visualization from the evidence explaining the outcome. Adapted here as a principle: show the comparison and its supporting measurements together.

credit: Original workshop comparison informed by observed measurement and evidence presentation.

title: Access window
summary: Show a route choice against its step-free access condition and a fixed train departure, with the remaining time margin visible.

layout.skeleton: Put the route drawing, the changed step-free entrance and the fixed departure on one continuous arrival line, followed by a compact route choice.
layout.focus: The actual access change and signed time margin before the specific train cutoff.
layout.desktop: Draw the active route from supplied locations and turns. Mark the step-free entrance that changed, then align its arrival time and the specific train departure so the remaining margin can be read directly.
layout.mobile: Keep the complete route evidence, changed step-free entrance, arrival time, signed margin and train departure in the immediate view. Keep route selection available there. Distinguish platform access from access to trains; claim neither without evidence.
layout.rhythm: Use a continuous route line, restrained station rules and one clear time break. Keep the evidence beside the route.

imagery.subject: An original route graphic derived only from supplied stops, entrance changes and times.
imagery.crop: Keep the changed entrance and deadline within the same visible route segment.
imagery.fallback: Use a text route with named steps and times when the brief lacks map geometry. Do not invent transfers, buffers or venue promises.

motion.trigger: The visitor selects a route or its recovery.
motion.effect: Trace only the supplied route segment and update the signed time margin beside the departure.
motion.reduced: Show the selected route and margin without animation.

action.instruction: Name the route choice and show the exact step-free access evidence and fixed train departure that support it.
action.label: Choose [route]

why: Arrival planning depends on access and a real deadline at once. A continuous route and explicit signed margin keep both conditions visible during selection or recovery.

sources.observation: Transport for London's step-free guide distinguishes step-free access to the platform from access to trains. The route drawing should preserve that distinction and state only the evidence supplied for the actual journey.

credit: Transport for London step-free route distinctions; original access-and-time composition.

title: Broadcast board
summary: Put the current program and the listener control in a single station masthead, with the schedule directly below.

layout.skeleton: Build one wide dark station band with the station name as a wordmark, followed by one program row and a full-width schedule strip. Align the three bands to a shared grid.
layout.focus: The current show title and the adjacent listener control. Present today's supplied schedule only once.
layout.desktop: Use the full top width for the masthead. Set the show title on the left and put the presenter, current state and listener control in the same aligned row at the far edge. Use ruled lines to connect them.
layout.mobile: Station, show title and host, listener control with visible state, then the schedule. Keep the complete control above the end of the first viewport when content fits.
layout.rhythm: Keep the broadcast data tightly grouped. Use a single larger break before the schedule. Keep desktop and narrow DOM order the same.

imagery.subject: An original status mark or small waveform attached to the listener control.
imagery.crop: No hero crop. Keep any mark inside the control or masthead with space around the program title.
imagery.fallback: Use type, ruled lines, a status word and a shape. Do not make up a broadcast frequency, schedule entry, or signal reading.

motion.trigger: the listener starts or stops the demo
motion.effect: Change the control's pressed state and show a brief sweep of the status mark.
motion.reduced: Update state and text instantly without animating the mark.

action.instruction: Expose a keyboard operable control next to a short state confirmation. Preserve any demo-only restriction and avoid autoplay.
action.label: Listen live

why: The station's identity comes from its current program and its listening action. A full-width program row gives the title the scale of an on-air board without borrowing the composition of a product launch.

sources.observation: KEXP's main PlayerControlTray and player launcher both expose a Listen Live button. The wording identifies the next action directly.

credit: KEXP live player, observed control wording. Original layout and color direction.

title: Service work order
summary: Make selection and the updating work order the page's visual focus. Integrate the price, current choice and turnaround in one receipt.

layout.skeleton: Lead with the work order. Set the service name and price on its first rule. Put the choice next to the result. Start the work order directly below the site header.
layout.focus: The actual booking controls and the selected value in the same work order.
layout.desktop: Use side-by-side choice and result columns under the service name. Fit the price, choice group and its live result within a 900 px viewport. Put supporting imagery and details below the work order.
layout.mobile: Keep the service title and price above a short native radio group and its result. At 360 px and below use two equal minmax(0,1fr) columns, 44 px targets and labels that wrap. At 320 × 700, fit the short group and its result with no scroll. With longer lists prioritize the selected option and its result.
layout.rhythm: Give the work order a short heading and comfortable control spacing. Let any decorative details follow the action.

imagery.subject: A small repair detail, drawn from the actual service in the brief.
imagery.crop: Crop to a functional detail and place it outside the choice and summary area.
imagery.fallback: A bordered label in the margin can carry one useful service fact from the brief. Omit it when the work order already contains the same fact.

motion.effect: Briefly emphasize the changed summary row and update the accessible status.
motion.reduced: Update the summary and accessible status immediately.

action.instruction: Use one labeled native group for a single selection. Update one visible polite status in the work order, and leave the service price and terms in place. Describe the actual selection state; show confirmation only when required by the brief.
action.label: Choose [day or option]

why: A work order has useful visual structure before it has branding. Putting the choice and its consequences in one composition keeps the service and task recognizable at a glance.

sources.observation: GOV.UK specifies radios when users can select only one option from a list.
The check-answers pattern uses a summary list with labels and values so users can verify what they entered.

credit: GOV.UK Design System radio and check-answers patterns. Original work-order layout and color direction.

title: Grouped details
summary: A compact worksheet for entering related facts together. A reader can find a field again by its group and its persistent label.

layout.skeleton: Set a short task title over a ruled worksheet. Include only the fields the task needs. Wrap related inputs in a fieldset with one visible legend. When there is just one group, its legend can supply the title.
layout.focus: The first field of the active group, aligned with its legend across the rule.
layout.desktop: Within 54rem, give short legends at least 12rem or the width of their text, and stack labeled controls in a right column up to 32rem wide. If the tracks no longer leave room for the inputs, move the legends over their fields. Start each group on a rule. Align the primary button with the inputs.
layout.mobile: At 390px use 16px side gutters, with each legend above its fields. Keep short task phrases and numeric ranges together. Adjust title size or break before the phrase if needed, and let longer text wrap. Read label, hint, input, then inline error. Put the action after the last field.
layout.rhythm: Use 16px input text in controls at least 44px high. Keep 4px from label to input, 12px between fields and 32px between fieldsets. Leave 24px before the primary button.

imagery.subject: The inputs carry the composition. Size each for its expected answer.
imagery.crop: For a short value, allow its expected character count plus padding. Longer text can use the available measure.
imagery.fallback: Plain native inputs and a 1px rule at each group boundary.

motion.trigger: The user submits the entered details.
motion.effect: Announce pending while sending. Keep values on failure and offer retry. On success, focus a confirmation heading describing the actual result and fade in the receipt text.
motion.reduced: Show the same result immediately with the same focus and announcement.

action.instruction: Name the button for its effect, such as ‘Save address’ or ‘Request repair’ when that operation is available. In a local preview, ‘Review answers’ opens the entered values with an Edit action. Show a receipt only after a successful submission.
action.label: [Task verb] [object]

why: Grouping by meaning lets someone check a related set of answers in one pass. Varying field widths gives a clue to the length of each answer.

sources.observation: USWDS places related controls in a fieldset with a named legend, keeps the controls in document order and aligns validation messages with their inputs.
The Address form example puts street, city, state and ZIP under one mailing-address legend. Each input has a visible label, and the ZIP input uses a shorter width.

credit: U.S. Web Design System, Form templates and Address form. The side legends, typography and colors are original.

title: One question
summary: Give one answer the width of a reading column. A large question leads directly into the response, with open paper on either side.

layout.skeleton: Make the question itself the heading and the field's label or the radio group's legend. Follow with one answer area. Include a Back link only when there is a previous step to revisit.
layout.focus: The question and its answer share one left edge. The question is the largest text on the surface.
layout.desktop: Start a 32rem column two grid tracks into a 12-column page. Set the question at 52px. Stack the supplied choices as labeled radio rows, or use one input when the answer is free text. Place the button against the same edge.
layout.mobile: At 390px use 20px side gutters and a 36px question. Order any real Back link, question, necessary hint, answer, inline correction, then the button. Let long labels wrap inside a tap target at least 44px high.
layout.rhythm: Leave 32px between the question block and the answer area. Separate choice rows by 8px and leave 24px before the primary button.

imagery.subject: The live answer is the visual element. A selected radio has a solid center as well as an accent outline.
imagery.crop: Let each answer label use the column width next to its control.
imagery.fallback: Use the browser's radio mark or a labeled text box.

motion.trigger: The reader activates the button after answering.
motion.effect: On a valid answer, focus the next question if there is one. On completion, focus a confirmation showing the accepted answer and fade in that text. Preserve the answer when the reader returns to edit it.
motion.reduced: Move focus and show the answer immediately.

action.instruction: Selecting a radio only changes the answer. Use native arrow-key navigation. Confirm the answer on activation and allow editing. Use ‘Continue’ only if a real next step opens.
action.label: Confirm answer

why: The eye and the keyboard reach the same decision in sequence. Making the heading do the work of the label lets the reader hear the question once.

sources.observation: GOV.UK shows the question serving as the main heading inside a legend for a group, or as the label for a single input. The answer controls and one forward action follow it.

credit: GOV.UK Design System, Question pages. The offset column, serif scale and plum palette are original.
